attributes.key_dependencies:
This proposal requires robust integration of on-chain and off-chain auditing to ensure transparency, accountability, and efficiency in treasury oversight for Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO. Key dependencies include access to funding data, technical infrastructure, benchmarking tools, and coordination with governance bodies. A structured framework is needed to monitor fund movements, detect redundant funding, and enforce accountability.

For on-chain auditing, tools like Oura and Dingo will extract transaction data from the Cardano blockchain. Premium APIs (Blockfrost, Koios, CardanoScan) will provide real-time access to transaction history. Lightweight nodes and cloud infrastructure will support the processing of large data sets. A transaction classification engine will trace ADA flows from Catalyst and Intersect, while clustering and graph analysis (Neo4j, NetworkX) will map wallet relationships and detect circular or suspicious fund flows. Integration with Xerberus SIREN will flag wallet addresses associated with fraud or abuse.

A public dashboard will visualize transaction clusters, risk scores, and fund movement, using tools like D3.js. This will provide transparency for governance bodies and the Cardano community. An automated reporting engine will generate periodic insights on fund performance, anomalies, and inefficiencies.

The off-chain component will verify deliverables, detect overlapping funding, and ensure cost-efficiency. A cross-referencing system will compare funding records from Catalyst and Intersect to detect double-dipping. Historical and current data will be required in standardized formats to enable automated checks. Industry benchmarks and market data subscriptions will assess if requested budgets align with typical costs for development, infrastructure, or events.

Collaboration with governance bodies and community reviewers is essential. Off-chain audits must go beyond milestone completion to evaluate cost-efficiency and financial transparency. Cloud-hosted pipelines and machine learning will support anomaly detection, exaggerated budgets, and project underperformance.

A unified treasury oversight dashboard will consolidate on-chain and off-chain data into a single interface, supporting real-time decision-making. This system will improve treasury integrity, prevent misuse, and ensure ADA is allocated to high-impact, verifiable projects—building long-term trust in Cardano’s funding ecosystem.
attributes.maintain_and_support:
This initiative is not just a one-time improvement but a foundation for permanent quality assurance in Project Catalyst, Intersect MBO, and any future Cardano treasury funding mechanisms. Our goal is to help teams achieve effective treasury fund usage, communicate their ROI to the community, and provide transparency in fund allocations, fostering community trust and long-term support for future funding rounds.

To ensure financial sustainability, we propose multiple paths. Intersect MBO or Catalyst could formally integrate this system, either rehiring us as the dedicated quality assurance team or incorporating the auditing framework into their governance structures. This would make funding oversight an ongoing process, ensuring treasury resources are used efficiently. Alternatively, if Intersect chooses to open-source the auditing tools and methodologies, we could provide consulting, implementation support, and technical maintenance services to governance bodies and funding programs that adopt this framework.

A service-based contract model could also sustain this effort, where Intersect, Catalyst, or other governance bodies pay for continuous auditing, financial oversight, and fund utilization reporting. This ensures real-time treasury monitoring, fraud prevention, and cost optimization remain active governance priorities. Additionally, treasury audit insights could generate revenue by providing customized funding analysis, risk assessments, and efficiency reports to governance stakeholders, reinforcing data-driven decision-making and trust in decentralized funding.

Beyond transparency, the data generated from these audits can be leveraged to support contract negotiations and reduce operational costs for Intersect MBO, Project Catalyst, and any other funding sources derived from the Cardano treasury. By identifying inefficiencies, eliminating redundant spending, and optimizing fund allocation strategies, this initiative ensures that Cardano’s governance bodies operate more efficiently while maintaining accountability and trust in treasury management.
attributes.proposal_description:
Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO collectively distribute millions of ADA to fund community-driven initiatives, yet there is no integrated on-chain and off-chain auditing system to ensure transparency, accountability, and efficient use of treasury funds. While on-chain tracking can offer visibility into fund movements, no unified system exists across funding programs to detect suspicious transactions, prevent self-dealing, or monitor post-disbursement activity. Off-chain auditing relies heavily on self-reported milestones assessed against proposer-defined KPIs, without independent evaluation of financial efficiency, redundant funding, or project impact.

Without an integrated framework, there is no way to track whether projects receive funding from multiple sources for the same deliverables. Catalyst and Intersect operate separately, with no cross-referencing of grants, allowing double-dipping and inefficient allocation. On-chain visibility doesn’t confirm how funds are used, and off-chain verification doesn’t assess if budgets are reasonable or if outcomes justify costs. Community participation in governance and oversight is limited by fragmented reporting, a lack of financial data, and no structured tools to evaluate funding efficiency.

This proposal introduces a dual-layer auditing system—on-chain financial tracking and off-chain deliverable verification. On-chain analysis will monitor fund flows, flag anomalies, and increase transparency. Off-chain audits will validate milestones, identify redundant funding, and evaluate cost-effectiveness. This integrated system provides governance bodies, working groups, and the community with real-time financial insights and clear reporting.

Governance bodies will gain structured tools to detect inefficiencies, refine funding models, and adjust policies based on data. Proposers will benefit from greater trust in a system that rewards transparency, filters out low-impact projects, and recognizes those that deliver real value. The broader community will be empowered with open data, improving decentralized decision-making.

Phased over nine months, this initiative starts with data collection and reporting, then expands into benchmarking and review of funded projects. The final phase delivers on-chain tools, public dashboards, and a sustainable, community-led oversight model. By preventing fund misallocation, reducing waste, and optimizing ROI, this system will enhance long-term sustainability and credibility
attributes.key_proposal_deliverables:
This 40-week initiative (Aug 2025–June 2026) will establish an integrated on-chain/off-chain auditing system to enhance financial transparency, accountability, and efficiency in Project Catalyst, Intersect MBO, and future Cardano Treasury programs.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Set up data pipelines, extract on-chain transactions, and structure a funding database of proposals, milestones, and distributions.
Done: Operational data system with clean, structured financial records.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Build transaction tracing and wallet clustering tools to identify fund flows, suspicious transfers, and self-dealing.
Done: Analysis engine maps movements and flags anomalies.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Develop risk scoring and pattern recognition models to detect loops, circular funding, and misalignments with off-chain data.
Done: Risk detection live, producing alerts and reports.

Phase 4 (Weeks 13–14): Integrate Xerberus SIREN for real-time fraud detection and wallet blacklist referencing.
Done: Real-time alerts on high-risk activity enabled.

Phase 5 (Weeks 15–18): Build a public-facing dashboard visualizing fund flows, risk scores, and treasury allocations.
Done: Dashboard live with real-time data and reports.

Phase 6 (Weeks 19–20): Full system testing and deployment with documentation and governance alignment.
Done: System live and governance-ready.

Phase 7 (Weeks 21–36): Off-chain audits of 2,000 Catalyst proposals and all Intersect grants.
	•	7.1 (Feb): 500 proposals, large Intersect grants audited, initial report delivered.
	•	7.2 (Mar): 500 more audits with ROI and impact analysis.
	•	7.3 (Apr): 500 audited with KPI and benchmarking models.
	•	7.4 (May): Final 500 audited, governance report + policy recommendations.
Done: 2,000 audits, impact analysis, and policy proposals delivered.

Phase 8 (Weeks 37–40): Propose long-term integration into Intersect MBO as a permanent oversight function.
Done: Transition plan and funding sustainability model completed.

Final Outcomes:
	•	Real-time on-chain fund tracking and risk analysis.
	•	Full off-chain audit of 2,000 proposals.
	•	ROI + cost benchmarking models.
	•	Treasury oversight dashboard.
	•	Policy improvements for fund allocation and milestone validation.
	•	Governance integration ensuring long-term audit sustainability.

This proposal delivers a complete, scalable solution for decentralized treasury auditing in Cardano.

attributes.problem_statement:
Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO distribute millions of ADA to fund community-driven initiatives, yet lack a comprehensive auditing system to ensure transparency, accountability, and efficient use of treasury funds. On-chain tracking is either missing or fragmented across funding programs, making it difficult to detect suspicious activity, prevent self-dealing, or monitor post-disbursement fund flows. Off-chain auditing, meanwhile, relies on self-reported milestone updates without independent verification of budget efficiency, redundant funding, or funding system integrity.

Without an integrated auditing framework, there is no structured way to detect double-dipping—when projects receive funding from multiple sources for the same deliverables. Since Catalyst and Intersect operate independently, there’s no cross-referencing of grants, which opens the door to inefficiencies and potential misuse. While on-chain systems can offer visibility into financial transactions, they fail to assess whether funds are spent as intended. Off-chain verification ensures milestone tracking, but lacks scrutiny into budget reasonability, optimal fund usage, or whether outcomes justify funding levels.

This lack of unified oversight limits community participation in governance and transparency. Without standardized reporting and shared financial insight, governance bodies and the broader community are unable to evaluate funding efficiency or assess project outcomes across funding cycles. The current process checks for delivery, but not financial accountability or funding optimization.

This proposal addresses these gaps by introducing a dual-layer auditing system—combining on-chain transaction analysis with off-chain deliverable audits. On-chain monitoring will track fund movement and detect anomalies in real-time. Off-chain auditing will independently verify milestones, flag redundant funding, and evaluate cost-effectiveness. Together, this framework will enable data-driven decision-making, strengthen community oversight, and ensure that treasury funds are allocated to high-impact, verifiable projects. By enhancing transparency, this system will build trust and integrity into Catalyst and Intersect’s funding mechanisms.
attributes.proposal_benefit:
Implementing a comprehensive on-chain and off-chain auditing system will significantly enhance transparency, accountability, and efficiency across Cardano’s major funding programs—Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO—delivering measurable value to all stakeholders. By ensuring that funds are effectively allocated, properly tracked, and independently verified, this initiative creates a data-driven governance framework that strengthens the integrity of Cardano’s treasury distribution, reduces inefficiencies, and maximizes long-term return on investment (ROI) for the community.

The Cardano Treasury, governance bodies, proposers, and the broader ecosystem will benefit from this enhanced oversight. By integrating on-chain financial tracking with off-chain verification of deliverables, this proposal ensures real-time visibility into fund movements and project performance, confirming that funded projects meet obligations without redundancy, inefficiency, or misuse of ADA.

For the Treasury, this reduces financial waste by detecting double-dipping and redundant funding across Catalyst and Intersect. Introducing cross-referenced funding data and cost-effectiveness assessments will optimize future allocations, enabling the treasury to fund more impactful projects while minimizing unnecessary spending.

Governance bodies, including Catalyst admins and Intersect committees, will gain a decision-making tool powered by structured financial insights. By tracking fund movements and verifying off-chain milestones against reasonable cost benchmarks, this system helps identify inefficiencies, refine funding models, and adjust policies based on actual performance.

Proposers benefit from fairness and credibility. Projects that deliver real value will be recognized and trusted by investors, partners, and the community. A unified auditing system eliminates low-value or fraudulent initiatives, reinforcing a merit-based funding environment.

The broader Cardano community gains access to open financial data and performance analytics. This empowers members to participate in governance discussions using verified insights rather than speculation, supporting stronger decentralized decision-making.

Ultimately, this initiative strengthens trust in Cardano’s funding ecosystem by ensuring every ADA is allocated responsibly, efficiently, and transparently—establishing Cardano as a leader in decentralized funding governance.
attributes.supplementary_endorsement:
This proposal has received endorsement from experienced Catalyst community members with a background in milestone review, proposal evaluation, and fraud detection. Below is a testimonial that highlights the need for a robust audit framework:

“In my experience as a Milestone Reviewer, I’ve encountered proposers attempting to submit fraudulent invoices, claim expenses with unverifiable company data, and push for fund release outside the established criteria. Off-chain validation is often difficult—some proposers manipulate data to appear legitimate, and on-chain validation without scrutiny can mask deeper issues.

As a Proposal Assessor, I’ve also tried to check whether projects had received funding outside Catalyst. One case was Cardax, a DEX that rugged despite having both Catalyst and private investment. Without cross-referencing off-chain funding or real-world deliverables, it’s easy to miss overlaps or redundancy.

Auditing shouldn’t just verify that code exists—it should analyze whether the work is original, whether budgets match deliverables, and whether proposers are using strawmen to bypass rules like the 5-proposal-per-person limit. I’ve seen cases where team members front proposals under different names, making it harder to track poor performance or abuse.

I’ve talked with others in the community about the importance of scrutiny—ideally not in the style of ‘witch hunts,’ but serious, structured oversight like what you’re proposing. We need frameworks that apply proportionate scrutiny—low-budget projects may not require deep audits, but higher-value proposals definitely should.

Between Funds 4 and 9, there was a Discord task force looking into review system abuse. We need something like that again. A dedicated audit group is essential in any decentralized system to track misuse and prevent treasury exploitation.

I strongly support this proposal. Without rigorous auditing, none of our strategic priorities matter. Treasury security must come first.”
— Anonymous Milestone Reviewer and Long-Term Catalyst Community Member

This endorsement illustrates the practical urgency behind establishing a permanent, scalable oversight system. The feedback aligns closely with our proposal’s design, which emphasizes proportional scrutiny, original work validation, and detection of redundant or deceptive funding behavior.

attributes.problem_statement:
Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO distribute millions of ADA to fund community-driven initiatives, yet lack a comprehensive auditing system to ensure transparency, accountability, and efficient use of treasury funds. On-chain tracking is either missing or fragmented across funding programs, making it difficult to detect suspicious activity, prevent self-dealing, or monitor post-disbursement fund flows. Off-chain auditing, meanwhile, relies on self-reported milestone updates without independent verification of budget efficiency, redundant funding, or funding system integrity.

Without an integrated auditing framework, there is no structured way to detect double-dipping—when projects receive funding from multiple sources for the same deliverables. Since Catalyst and Intersect operate independently, there’s no cross-referencing of grants, which opens the door to inefficiencies and potential misuse. While on-chain systems can offer visibility into financial transactions, they fail to assess whether funds are spent as intended. Off-chain verification ensures milestone tracking, but lacks scrutiny into budget reasonability, optimal fund usage, or whether outcomes justify funding levels.

This lack of unified oversight limits community participation in governance and transparency. Without standardized reporting and shared financial insight, governance bodies and the broader community are unable to evaluate funding efficiency or assess project outcomes across funding cycles. The current process checks for delivery, but not financial accountability or funding optimization.

This proposal addresses these gaps by introducing a dual-layer auditing system—combining on-chain transaction analysis with off-chain deliverable audits. On-chain monitoring will track fund movement and detect anomalies in real-time. Off-chain auditing will independently verify milestones, flag redundant funding, and evaluate cost-effectiveness. Together, this framework will enable data-driven decision-making, strengthen community oversight, and ensure that treasury funds are allocated to high-impact, verifiable projects. By enhancing transparency, this system will build trust and integrity into Catalyst and Intersect’s funding mechanisms.

attributes.supplementary_endorsement:

attributes.problem_statement:
Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO distribute millions of ADA to fund community-driven initiatives, yet lack a comprehensive auditing system to ensure transparency, accountability, and efficient use of treasury funds. On-chain tracking is either missing or fragmented across funding programs, making it difficult to detect suspicious activity, prevent self-dealing, or monitor post-disbursement fund flows. Off-chain auditing, meanwhile, relies on self-reported milestone updates without independent verification of budget efficiency, redundant funding, or funding system integrity.

Without an integrated auditing framework, there is no structured way to detect double-dipping—when projects receive funding from multiple sources for the same deliverables. Since Catalyst and Intersect operate independently, there’s no cross-referencing of grants, which opens the door to inefficiencies and potential misuse. While on-chain systems can offer visibility into financial transactions, they fail to assess whether funds are spent as intended. Off-chain verification ensures milestone tracking, but lacks scrutiny into budget reasonability, optimal fund usage, or whether outcomes justify funding levels.

This lack of unified oversight limits community participation in governance and transparency. Without standardized reporting and shared financial insight, governance bodies and the broader community are unable to evaluate funding efficiency or assess project outcomes across funding cycles. The current process checks for delivery, but not financial accountability or funding optimization.

This proposal addresses these gaps by introducing a dual-layer auditing system—combining on-chain transaction analysis with off-chain deliverable audits. On-chain monitoring will track fund movement and detect anomalies in real-time. Off-chain auditing will independently verify milestones, flag redundant funding, and evaluate cost-effectiveness. Together, this framework will enable data-driven decision-making, strengthen community oversight, and ensure that treasury funds are allocated to high-impact, verifiable projects. By enhancing transparency, this system will build trust and integrity into Catalyst and Intersect’s funding mechanisms.

attributes.key_dependencies:
The successful implementation of this proposal requires a robust integration of on-chain and off-chain auditing components to ensure transparency, accountability, and efficiency in treasury oversight for Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO. These dependencies span technical infrastructure, access to funding data, collaboration with governance bodies, benchmarking tools, and advanced data processing capabilities. A well-structured framework must be established to ensure that funds are transparently tracked, redundant funding is identified, and financial oversight is effectively enforced.

For the on-chain component, the Catalyst and Intersect MBO auditing system depends on data extraction and processing tools to analyze the movement of treasury funds post-disbursement. This requires the use of lightweight nodes and data indexers such as Oura and Dingo to extract and process transaction data from the Cardano blockchain. Additionally, access to premium API tiers for services like Blockfrost, Koios, and CardanoScan is critical for real-time and historical blockchain transaction tracking. These tools will provide the necessary infrastructure to monitor fund movement, identify self-dealing transactions, and detect suspicious patterns. Furthermore, high-performance cloud computing resources will be required to efficiently process large-scale blockchain transaction data, ensuring the timely generation of reports and insights for governance bodies and the broader community.

A key part of the on-chain auditing process involves advanced blockchain analysis and pattern detection techniques. The proposal relies on the development of a transaction classification engine that traces ADA flows originating from Catalyst and Intersect MBO disbursements, enabling governance bodies to monitor how funds are used after allocation. Additionally, clustering and network analysis using graph-based tools such as Neo4j and NetworkX will be necessary to map wallet relationships, detect circular transactions, and identify instances of fund redirection that suggest potential collusion or self-dealing. To further enhance security, integration with Xerberus SIREN will allow the system to cross-reference wallet addresses with known fraudulent activity databases, helping to prevent funds from being directed toward malicious actors.

For effective transparency and community engagement, a public reporting and visualization tool must be developed. This requires the creation of an interactive dashboard using technologies such as D3.js, which will provide aggregated fund flow analytics for the Cardano community, governance bodies, and other stakeholders. The dashboard will display transaction clusters, risk scores, and financial movement patterns, allowing for easier identification of inefficiencies. An automated reporting engine will be developed to generate periodic treasury oversight reports, providing real-time insights into Catalyst and Intersect MBO funding patterns. These reports will highlight any anomalies detected, ensuring that governance committees and community members have access to actionable intelligence.

In addition to the on-chain tracking component, a robust off-chain treasury oversight framework is required to verify project deliverables, prevent redundant funding, and ensure cost-effectiveness. One of the primary dependencies for this component is a cross-referencing system that identifies projects receiving multiple sources of funding for the same deliverables. This requires structured access to historical and current funding records from Catalyst and Intersect MBO, allowing the system to detect overlaps and prevent unnecessary treasury allocations. Developing an automated detection mechanism will streamline the identification of projects that may be receiving excess funding or misrepresenting their financial needs.

Another critical dependency is the integration of cost benchmarking and industry research tools to evaluate whether project budgets align with real-world pricing. Subscription-based market research platforms will be used to analyze standard costs associated with software development, infrastructure, event management, and other project types. These tools will ensure that requested budgets are proportional to the scope of work, reducing instances of excessive funding requests. Comparative analysis models will be used to cross-reference Catalyst and Intersect-funded initiatives with similar projects in the broader industry, providing an objective assessment of whether treasury allocations are justified.

To ensure off-chain verification processes align with Catalyst and Intersect MBO’s existing governance structures, collaboration with community reviewers and proposal verification teams is necessary. Governance bodies and funding committees must integrate financial audit processes into their milestone assessment frameworks, ensuring that off-chain verification extends beyond basic milestone completion to include financial transparency and efficiency assessments. This will help bridge the gap between self-reported project milestones and real financial accountability, making it more difficult for low-value or fraudulent projects to cycle through multiple funding rounds without delivering meaningful impact.

Another key dependency is the development of a public reporting and treasury oversight dashboard that consolidates both on-chain and off-chain insights into a single interface. This web-based platform will provide the broader Cardano community with access to funding efficiency metrics, redundant funding detection reports, and cost-effectiveness analyses. To enhance accessibility, the dashboard will include automated deliverable audits, incorporating data from community reviews, milestone completion records, and financial tracking insights. These structured reports will ensure that governance bodies, funding committees, and community members can make data-driven decisions when evaluating treasury allocations.

To power the off-chain analysis component, cloud-hosted data processing pipelines will be required for analyzing funding records, cost benchmarks, and redundant funding detections. AWS high-performance computing resources will provide the infrastructure for large-scale data analytics, enabling efficient processing of treasury allocation data. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be employed to detect anomalies in funding requests, highlight exaggerated budgets, and flag underperforming projects. AI-driven risk assessment models will allow governance bodies to prioritize high-risk proposals for further review, strengthening the accountability of Catalyst and Intersect MBO’s funding mechanisms.

One of the biggest challenges this initiative faces is ensuring that all necessary funding data is accessible while maintaining compliance with privacy regulations. Project records from Catalyst and Intersect MBO must be made available in a structured, standardized format, ensuring seamless integration into the auditing framework. Governance bodies must collaborate to create data-sharing agreements that balance transparency with the protection of sensitive project information. Additionally, the initiative must ensure scalability and computational efficiency, as processing large volumes of transaction data and proposal records will require optimized indexing techniques to maintain real-time analytics capabilities.

Resistance from certain funded projects could also pose a challenge, as some proposers may be reluctant to subject their financials to external auditing. Clear communication on the benefits of financial transparency and accountability will be critical to gaining broader support from the Cardano community. Governance bodies must enforce participation in financial audits as a condition for receiving treasury funds, ensuring that all funded projects comply with reporting and verification requirements.

Finally, the initiative must be fully integrated with decentralized oversight models, ensuring that community members can actively contribute to fraud detection and governance improvements. The auditing framework must align with existing governance processes while also introducing new tools for community-driven financial oversight. Publicly accessible reports, interactive audit dashboards, and treasury efficiency scores will allow the broader ecosystem to monitor funding patterns, strengthening decentralized decision-making in Cardano’s treasury management.

By addressing these dependencies, this proposal will establish a robust, independent, and transparent auditing system that improves treasury oversight, optimizes ADA allocations, and strengthens trust in Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO’s funding mechanisms. The successful integration of on-chain financial tracking and off-chain deliverable auditing will create a comprehensive governance tool that prevents redundant funding, detects financial inefficiencies, and ensures that treasury funds are used effectively.

attributes.proposal_description:
Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO collectively distribute millions of ADA to fund community-driven initiatives, yet there is no comprehensive on-chain and off-chain auditing system to ensure transparency, accountability, and the effective use of treasury funds. While on-chain tracking mechanisms could provide visibility into fund movements, they do not exist in a structured or unified manner across all funding programs, leaving significant gaps in detecting suspicious transactions, preventing self-dealing, and monitoring how funds flow post-disbursement. At the same time, off-chain auditing and deliverable verification rely heavily on self-reported milestone updates, which are assessed only against proposer-defined KPIs without independent evaluation of financial efficiency, redundant funding, or overall funding system integrity. Without an integrated on-chain and off-chain framework, there is no structured way to track whether projects receive multiple sources of funding for the same deliverables, leading to double-dipping and inefficient allocation of resources across Catalyst and Intersect. Since these funding bodies operate separately, there is no system that cross-references grants to prevent redundant funding, resulting in treasury inefficiencies and potential misuse.

While on-chain transparency could offer insight into financial flows, without off-chain verification, there is no way to determine whether funds are spent as intended or whether deliverables match the funding received. Similarly, while off-chain verification ensures that projects report milestones, it does not assess whether requested budgets were reasonable, whether funds were used optimally, or whether the project outcomes justify the amount allocated. The lack of a structured on-chain and off-chain oversight mechanism also limits community participation in governance and financial oversight. Without on-chain tracking, there is no unified visibility into treasury distributions and fund movements after disbursement, preventing detection of collusion, self-dealing, and fund mismanagement. Meanwhile, off-chain reporting remains fragmented and non-standardized, with no structured method for governance bodies, working groups, or the community to evaluate funding efficiency or track project outcomes across funding cycles. This results in a funding ecosystem where approvals and milestone completions are checked but financial accountability, cost-effectiveness, and funding system optimization remain unaddressed.

To bridge these gaps, this proposal introduces an integrated on-chain and off-chain auditing system that ensures full transparency in fund allocation, movement, and project execution across all major Cardano funding programs. By leveraging on-chain analysis to monitor financial flows and prevent transaction-level inefficiencies while implementing off-chain audits to verify deliverables, prevent redundant funding, and ensure cost-effectiveness, this initiative will create a fully transparent and data-driven funding framework. This dual-layered approach will provide governance bodies, working groups, and the Cardano community with accurate financial insights and real-time reporting, enabling better decision-making, stronger accountability, and an optimized funding system that ensures ADA is allocated to projects that deliver measurable, verifiable impact.

The current verification mechanisms in Project Catalyst and Intersect rely on self-reported milestones that do not provide any financial accountability beyond confirming whether deliverables match the proposer’s commitments. However, funding inefficiencies persist because there is no system to determine whether proposers received redundant funding, no independent evaluation of whether requested budgets were proportionate to project impact, and no tracking of how funds are actually spent once disbursed. Treasury inefficiencies and double-dipping occur because there is no cross-referencing of grants across different funding programs. If a project receives Catalyst funding and later secures a grant from Intersect for the same deliverable, there is no structured mechanism to flag or prevent such an occurrence. Without financial tracking after disbursement, there is no accountability on how funds are allocated, whether they are being used effectively, or if a project is merely securing funding without producing tangible results.

Off-chain auditing processes focus entirely on whether projects meet proposer-defined KPIs, but these KPIs are often vague, making it possible for projects to claim milestone completion with minimal effort. For example, a project that commits to creating an MVP could submit a non-functional prototype and still claim to have completed the milestone. This is because the verification process does not include an evaluation of impact, cost efficiency, or whether deliverables justify the funding received. On-chain transparency is also lacking, as fund movements post-disbursement are not monitored. Without financial tracking, treasury oversight is limited, and governance bodies have no clear data to refine funding strategies, making it impossible to detect waste, inefficiencies, or potential fraud.

By implementing a comprehensive auditing system that integrates both on-chain financial tracking and off-chain deliverable verification, this proposal ensures that funds are used efficiently and that projects provide meaningful value to the Cardano ecosystem. The introduction of on-chain fund tracking will provide visibility into treasury transactions, allowing governance bodies to identify and prevent cases of self-dealing or misallocated funds. Additionally, off-chain auditing will validate project deliverables against a structured cost-effectiveness framework to ensure that treasury funds are used optimally. This means funding decisions will no longer be based solely on self-reported updates but on objective assessments of financial accountability and project impact.

For governance bodies and working groups, this initiative provides structured financial insights that will enhance decision-making. On-chain tracking will allow governance entities to monitor fund movements and detect irregularities, while off-chain audits will provide a comprehensive assessment of project effectiveness. This system will allow Catalyst and Intersect to refine their funding strategies, ensure that treasury allocations align with ecosystem growth goals, and prevent redundant funding cycles that weaken treasury sustainability. Governance entities will also benefit from public reporting tools that provide transparency in fund distribution, allowing the community to hold projects accountable and engage in decentralized oversight.

Proposers will also benefit from a more transparent funding model. Currently, skepticism exists regarding treasury funding due to instances of misallocated funds, redundant projects, and minimal accountability for low-impact initiatives. By introducing a structured auditing process, legitimate projects will be able to demonstrate transparency and efficiency, strengthening their credibility within the Cardano ecosystem. This will also ensure that proposers who genuinely contribute value are prioritized in future funding rounds, preventing funds from being disproportionately allocated to initiatives that fail to deliver measurable impact.

The broader Cardano community will gain access to open financial reporting and analytics, enabling decentralized participation in treasury oversight. The availability of transparent financial data will allow community members to engage in governance discussions with accurate information, fostering informed decision-making. This will increase trust in treasury funding mechanisms, ensuring that funding decisions are not driven by speculation but by verifiable financial data.

From an ROI perspective, the implementation of this system will significantly improve the long-term sustainability of the Cardano Treasury. By reducing redundant funding, optimizing cost-effectiveness, and ensuring that each ADA allocated is used efficiently, this initiative will allow treasury funds to support more projects without increasing overall expenditures. Over time, the elimination of fund misallocation and inefficiencies could save millions of ADA, extending the usability of the treasury while maximizing the impact of funded initiatives. This optimization will position Cardano as a leader in decentralized funding governance, ensuring that funding programs are not only transparent but also aligned with long-term ecosystem sustainability.

To ensure successful implementation, this initiative will be executed in structured phases over a nine-month period. The first phase will focus on data collection and initial reporting, gathering funding records from Catalyst and Intersect to identify patterns of redundant funding and inefficiencies. Initial reports will be published to provide insights into treasury fund flow analysis. The second phase will expand on these findings by conducting a detailed review of funded projects, introducing cost benchmarks, and providing structured insights to governance bodies to improve funding models. The final phase will deliver a comprehensive final report with policy recommendations, implement on-chain tracking mechanisms, and establish a long-term community-led financial oversight framework to ensure continuous treasury optimization.

By introducing an integrated on-chain and off-chain auditing system, this proposal provides a long-term solution to inefficiencies in Cardano’s funding ecosystem. Strengthening financial tracking, deliverable verification, and treasury oversight will ensure that funding is allocated responsibly, redundant funding is eliminated, and treasury resources are used in the most impactful way possible. This initiative is not only about improving past funding cycles but about building a more sustainable, transparent, and data-driven governance framework that benefits the entire Cardano community.

attributes.problem_statement:
Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO collectively distribute millions of ADA to fund community-driven initiatives, yet there is no comprehensive on-chain and off-chain auditing system to ensure transparency, accountability, and the effective use of treasury funds. While on-chain tracking mechanisms could provide visibility into fund movements, they do not exist in a structured or unified manner across all funding programs, leaving significant gaps in detecting suspicious transactions, preventing self-dealing, and monitoring how funds flow post-disbursement. At the same time, off-chain auditing and deliverable verification rely heavily on self-reported milestone updates, which are assessed only against proposer-defined KPIs without independent evaluation of financial efficiency, redundant funding, or overall funding system integrity.

Without an integrated on-chain and off-chain framework, there is no structured way to track whether projects receive multiple sources of funding for the same deliverables, leading to double-dipping and inefficient allocation of resources across Catalyst and Intersect. Since these funding bodies operate separately, there is no system that cross-references grants to prevent redundant funding, resulting in treasury inefficiencies and potential misuse. While on-chain transparency could offer insight into financial flows, without off-chain verification, there is no way to determine whether funds are spent as intended or whether deliverables match the funding received. Similarly, while off-chain verification ensures that projects report milestones, it does not assess whether requested budgets were reasonable, whether funds were used optimally, or whether project outcomes justify the amount allocated.

The lack of a structured on-chain and off-chain oversight mechanism also limits community participation in governance and financial oversight. Without on-chain tracking, there is no unified visibility into treasury distributions and fund movements after disbursement, preventing detection of collusion, self-dealing, and fund mismanagement. Meanwhile, off-chain reporting remains fragmented and non-standardized, with no structured method for governance bodies, working groups, or the community to evaluate funding efficiency or track project outcomes across funding cycles. This results in a funding ecosystem where approvals and milestone completions are checked but financial accountability, cost-effectiveness, and funding system optimization remain unaddressed.

To bridge these gaps, this proposal introduces an integrated on-chain and off-chain auditing system that ensures full transparency in fund allocation, movement, and project execution across Project Catalyst and Intersect. By leveraging on-chain analysis to monitor financial flows and prevent transaction-level inefficiencies while implementing off-chain audits to verify deliverables, prevent redundant funding, and ensure cost-effectiveness, this initiative will create a fully transparent and data-driven funding framework. This dual-layered approach will provide governance bodies, working groups, and the Cardano community with accurate financial insights and real-time reporting, enabling better decision-making, stronger accountability, and an optimized funding system that ensures ADA is allocated to projects that deliver measurable, verifiable impact.
attributes.proposal_benefit:
Implementing a comprehensive on-chain and off-chain auditing system will significantly enhance transparency, accountability, and efficiency across Cardano’s major funding programs—Project Catalyst and Intersect MBO—providing measurable benefits to multiple stakeholders within the ecosystem. By ensuring that funding is effectively allocated, properly tracked, and independently verified, this initiative will create a data-driven governance framework that strengthens the integrity of Cardano’s treasury distribution, reduces inefficiencies, and maximizes the long-term return on investment (ROI) for the entire community.

The Cardano Treasury, governance bodies, proposers, and the broader community will all benefit from the enhanced financial oversight and streamlined funding mechanisms enabled by this initiative. By integrating on-chain financial tracking with off-chain verification of deliverables, the proposal provides real-time insights into fund movements and milestone performance, ensuring that funded projects meet their obligations without redundancy, inefficiency, or misuse of ADA.

For the Cardano Treasury, this initiative reduces financial waste by detecting double-dipping and redundant funding across Catalyst and Intersect, ensuring that treasury funds are only allocated where they are truly needed. By introducing cross-referenced funding data and cost-effectiveness assessments, the system will optimize future treasury allocations, allowing the treasury to fund more projects with higher impact while reducing unnecessary spending.

For governance bodies, including Catalyst administrators and Intersect committees, the auditing framework will serve as a decision-making tool that provides structured financial insights. By tracking fund movements on-chain and verifying off-chain deliverables against reasonable cost benchmarks, this system allows governance bodies to identify systemic inefficiencies, adjust funding models, and refine policies based on actual financial performance data. This means future funding cycles will be more transparent, data-driven, and resistant to abuse.

For funded proposers, the new auditing system enhances credibility and trust in the funding process. By ensuring all funding applications are held to the same standard of accountability, legitimate projects that deliver value will be recognized, fairly evaluated, and able to demonstrate transparency to potential investors, partners, and the wider ecosystem. The system also helps reduce skepticism around treasury-funded initiatives by eliminating fraudulent or low-value projects, ensuring that well-intended proposers compete on merit rather than exploitation of gaps in oversight.

For the broader Cardano community, this initiative empowers community members by providing open-access reports and analytics on treasury spending, project performance, and funding efficiency. By making financial data transparent and accessible, this system allows the entire ecosystem to participate in governance discussions with accurate data rather than speculation, strengthening decentralized decision-making.

From an ROI perspective, this initiative preserves and optimizes ADA treasury funds by eliminating inefficiencies, preventing fund misallocation, and ensuring every ADA spent generates maximum value. The financial insights generated will inform smarter, more efficient treasury distribution in future funding rounds, leading to higher-impact projects and more sustainable ecosystem growth. Over time, reducing redundant funding, improving cost-effectiveness, and preventing fund leakage could save millions of ADA, extending the lifespan and usability of the Cardano Treasury while increasing the trustworthiness and effectiveness of the funding ecosystem.

Ultimately, this proposal establishes Cardano as a leader in decentralized, transparent, and efficient funding governance, reinforcing the credibility of its grant distribution programs while ensuring every treasury ADA is put to its best possible use.
